description: A kilogram of a source list's coal reaches an EF 3.1 energy flow through a mapping that states one number, `qudt:conversionMultiplier`. Until #407 that number was typed by hand as a `conversion_factor` on a row of the list's match overrides, with no unit, no net-or-gross basis and no provenance beyond a comment, and the same heating value was written four times for four lists. It is now derived from a property statement the list makes about its own flow (`<list>-property-statements.json`): one kilogram of AGRIBALYSE's hard coal is 18.2 MJ of net calorific value, one of Stepwise's is 19.1 MJ of gross calorific value, one of ecoinvent's is 18.01 MJ of calorific value whose basis the workbook does not state. The multipliers do not move -- every claim below holds the number the build of `5f06833` (24 October 2026, the merge base) published -- and the basis moves to `flow-property`, with the quantity the number came through published beside it. A mapping still stating `curated` or `correspondence-table` for one of these rows means the merge read the override instead of the flow.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's hard coal in the ground converts onto Hard Coal at its own lower heating value, 18.2 MJ/kg, derived from a property of the flow
expectations.comment: The issue's example row. The substance block at the end of `AGB32_final.CSV` gives this coal a lower heating value of 18.2 MJ/kg, and EF 3.1's `Hard Coal` is measured in net calorific value, so the net statement is the one the merge chooses. On the build of `5f06833` the same 18.2 was published with basis `curated`, read off the override row. Phase B of #407 reads the substance block off the CSV, but this one line is misspelt in the vendor's file (`18.2 MH/kg`), so the adapter leaves it unread and the net value stays a curated statement saying so; the flow also carries the vendor's gross 19.1, read off the same comment. Brown coal beside it is the vendor's own 8.75.

expectations.title: Stepwise 2006's hard coal converts onto Hard Coal at the 19.1 MJ/kg its own method counts a kilogram as, by the list's stated rule
expectations.comment: Stepwise's `Non-renewable energy` factor for this row is 19.1, which is also the `Higher heating value (HHV)` its substance block states; EF's flow is net. Since phase B the adapter reads both off the export -- the method's number as a `calorific-value` of unstated basis stated by the method, the block's as a gross calorific value stated by the flow -- and the number lands because `stepwise-2006-property-statements.json` carries a conversion rule saying a Stepwise row converts onto net by the method's number, ahead of any closer statement; the mapping publishes `conversion_quantity` as the calorific-value IRI and its provenance names `Stepwise2006_v1.09.csv`. Whether Stepwise should convert by the net value instead (18.2, making its factor 1.05 per MJ) is a measured change of its own; this claim pins that neither phase made it.

expectations.title: ecoinvent 3.8's crude oil converts at 42.3 MJ/kg, the release's own value, from a per-release property statement
expectations.comment: #162's vintage rule survives the move: 3.8's exchange carries no heating value, so `ecoinvent-property-statements.json` states 42.3 for 3.8 and names 3.9.1 to 3.12 in `stated_by_vendor_in`, where the exchange's own `heating value, net` property (43.4) is what the adapter reads onto the flow. A 43.4 here would mean the per-release value was lost.

expectations.title: BAFU's crude oil converts at 43.1 MJ/kg, the ratio its own archive states, from a property statement
expectations.comment: The one BAFU carrier whose number is BAFU's own rather than ecoinvent's. The statement is `calorific-value` with the basis unstated, because the dataset ratio says nothing about net or gross, and it converts onto EF's net flow with the mapping saying the basis was unstated.
